points.text: States that most energy is lost as heat, in egestion and excretion, and in uneaten or undigested parts
Explains that only about a tenth is built into new tissue that the next level can eat

items.prompt: Explain why only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next level, and what happens to the rest.

points.text: States that energy flows one way, sunlight in and heat out, while carbon cycles
Explains that photosynthesis draws CO2 into plants while respiration, combustion and decomposition return CO2 to the air

items.prompt: Compare how energy and carbon move through an ecosystem: state which one cycles and which flows one way, naming the processes involved.

points.text: States that chloroplasts trap light energy to make sugar in photosynthesis
Explains that mitochondria release energy from that sugar as ATP in aerobic respiration, which continues day and night

items.prompt: A leaf cell contains both chloroplasts and mitochondria. Explain, in terms of photosynthesis and respiration, why it needs both.

points.text: States a phospholipid bilayer with hydrophilic heads facing outward and hydrophobic tails inside, with proteins drifting through it
Explains that channel proteins allow only selected substances to cross

items.prompt: Describe the structure of the cell membrane in the fluid mosaic model and explain how that structure makes it selectively permeable.

levels.descriptor: Methods are chosen and applied exactly, the 10% rule and the energy-carbon contrast are stated explicitly, leaf-cell and membrane steps are described with chloroplasts, mitochondria, heads, tails and channel proteins, and conclusions are justified without claiming energy is recycled through the ecosystem.
levels.label: Secure

levels.descriptor: Method is correct in outline but a 10% step, carbon-cycle step, leaf-cell step or membrane step is skipped.
levels.label: Developing

levels.descriptor: Methods are misapplied - for example claiming energy is recycled through the ecosystem because matter cycles - and the working does not support the answer.
levels.label: Beginning
